svg.text: End-to-end architecture from governance through recovery · ai-agent-iam-blueprint
Business value × Required autonomy × Potential blast radius
what is logged · what can be stopped
Agent risk tier · Launch gates · Approval boundaries · Acceptable risk definition · Autonomy expansion criteria
• attack both agent layer and infrastructure
An agent observes outcomes and adapts. Its authority must therefore be constrained externally, not inside its own reasoning.
May dynamically choose how to pursue a goal
Cannot authorize itself or expand its own access
Cannot bypass policy or self-delegate authority
Its reasoning may adapt. Its authority must not.
Manipulated input → legitimate tool → observe outcome → next tool → adapt toward corrupted objective
agent ID · delegated user · task · tool · action · resource · retrieved context
• acting as itself or for a user
Every agent has a registered identity, a named owner, and an approved scope before it may act.
No anonymous agents · No agent acts beyond its registered purpose · No shared credentials
Tool Gateway / External Policy Enforcement Point — every proposed tool call passes through this layer
• Is the agent registered and active?
• Is the delegated authority valid and in scope?
• Is the tool on the agent's approved list?
• Is the action permitted within that tool?
• Is the data within approved scope and classification?
• Has volume or transaction risk crossed a threshold?
• Was prompt injection or suspicious context detected?
• Does separation of duties require another approver?
• Has the agent been auto-suspended for prior denials?
The model proposes. This layer authorizes.
Collect all violations before resolving · DENY overrides APPROVAL_REQUIRED overrides ALLOW
Cloud versus on-premises is not the trust boundary.
Identity, policy and enforced authority are the trust boundary.
Agents cross deployment boundaries by design. The enforcement point must travel with the identity.
• same IAM controls apply to defense agents
AI assists investigation. It does not approve its own containment powers.
Defending the enterprise from AI · Using AI to defend the enterprise · Both require the same identity and policy controls
A security agent is not trusted because its stated purpose is security. It is trusted because its identity and authority are verified.
SHA-256 hash-chained audit log · Auto-suspend on denial threshold · Every decision recorded at evaluation time
• suspend the agent · revoke credentials · terminate sessions · disable specific tools
• quarantine malicious content · identify affected identities and systems
• reconstruct the attack path · roll back where possible · update policies and controls
No agent restores itself. No tool re-enables itself. Human approval gate at every recovery step.
Evidence from response updates risk tiers, policy thresholds and product design for the next deployment decision.
Recovery is complete only when root cause is understood and policy is updated to prevent recurrence.
operational evidence feeds back into risk tiering · product design · policy · GTM strategy
